collection.description: An elder's story of getting lost as a child has grown with every telling: keep telling it, or tell the plain version.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is telling (friend) about the time (subject.he/she) got lost in the jungle as a child. In this version there was a storm, a cliff, a mysterious glowing frog, and (subject) found the way home by following the stars. (friend) is spellbound. Somewhere in the back of (subject)'s mind, a small voice points out that last year there was no frog, and the year before there was no cliff.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: The glowing frog leads young (subject) to a hidden waterfall. (friend) gasps. "Is that TRUE?" (subject) thinks about it honestly. "Parts of it," (subject.he/she) says. "I really did get lost. And I really did find my way home." (friend) decides those are the most important parts anyway.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: "Actually," (subject) says, "I got lost behind the gardens for an afternoon and cried until my mother found me." (friend) stares. "That's it?" "That's it." (friend) thinks about this. "Was there a frog?" (subject) smiles. "There might have been a small one."
